analyst_view.overall: Arsenal are 3rd in the league phase on 10 points and top of the Premier League despite Saturday's 2-2 draw at Newcastle; Dortmund are 12th on 9 points and top of the Bundesliga after a 1-0 win at Gladbach. Goalkeeper David Raya went off at Newcastle with a shoulder injury and was due an MRI; Arteta called it 'not good', and one preview already lists him out, so Kepa is likely to start. Dortmund's main striker Serhou Guirassy is still nursing a thigh/hamstring problem and his status may not be known until matchday, while Carney Chukwuemeka needs a late fitness test. The numbers already take about 10% off Arsenal's goals for Saka and count both sides' recent form, but they do not know about Zubimendi, Raya or Guirassy. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take about 10% off Arsenal for Saka's absence, so I do not size him again. What they don't know is that Guirassy, Dortmund's main striker, has missed every game since early November and is still a matchday doubt, with Fabio Silva leading the line at Gladbach. Raya's likely absence helps Dortmund a little, so the net trim is small: 2.4 x 0.97, about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Arsenal around 6.3 and Dortmund's busier recent corner count already in (+3%). Arsenal build corners from sustained pressure and set pieces even without Saka, and Dortmund tend to defend deep away from home, which is in both teams' records already. Neither Raya's nor Guirassy's absence changes that much, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already add about 13% to Arsenal for their high recent card count, with Dortmund's quieter run counted too (-3%). No referee has been named, neither side has a ban, and there is no history of needle between these clubs that the numbers miss. I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Dortmund's busy recent shooting already counted (+11%). Without a fit Guirassy, Dortmund have fewer shots from inside the box, and Arsenal miss Zubimendi's control in midfield as well as Saka out wide. I trim slightly: 24.9 x 0.98, about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, including a small boost for Dortmund's recent accuracy (+3%). Guirassy is Dortmund's most clinical finisher and is unlikely to be fully fit even if he plays, and Arsenal have been less incisive while Saka is out. I go a little lower, to about 8.3.
